Alex K: quick check — I merged the TF change that moves service secrets into k8s (moves from app-managed -> ExternalSecrets mapping). pods for `payments-service` didn't pick up the rotated key after I applied. anyone seen this pattern?

Priya S: did you update the ExternalSecret resource or just the TF module?

Alex K: updated both. TF now creates a k8s secret named `payments-sa-keys` and ExternalSecret maps `secretKey` -> `credentials`. ExternalSecrets controller shows sync success but pod env still old value.

Ben L: might be that the secret object changed but deployment doesn't restart. k8s won't re-inject env vars for running pods. did you add an annotation checksum on the deployment to trigger rollout?

Alex K: not yet. trying to understand why the ExternalSecret controller didn't trigger a rolling update (we have `refreshInterval` default). logs show: `synced ExternalSecret payments/epayments  --> secret payments-sa-keys (unchanged)` even though the secret data did change in Vault.

devops-bot: CI: terraform/apply succeeded for `infra/k8s/payments` (plan: 3 to add, 1 to change). (deployment) (checks: passed)

Priya S: possible that Vault rotation created a new version but the secret content bytes are same base64-wise? or ExternalSecrets uses annotations to decide if it needs to update `secret.data` field. can you paste the ExternalSecret yaml?

Alex K: pasted snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: payments-es
  namespace: payments
spec:
  refreshInterval: "1m"
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault-store
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
  target:
    name: payments-sa-keys
  data:
  - secretKey: credentials
    remoteRef:
      key: secret/data/services/payments/sa
      property: credentials
```

Tara M: that looks fine. where is the TF that creates the k8s secret? if ES is creating the secret, TF shouldn't also be managing it (conflict).

Alex K: TF used to create the secret, but I changed to let ExternalSecrets own it. I removed the k8s_secret resource and added the ES above. TF apply removed the old secret resource and created the ES.

Sam R: when you delete and recreate the secret name, sometimes the controller does a replace and the deployment's `.spec.template` doesn't change, so pods aren't restarted. common pattern: add `checksum/config` annotation on the deployment template with a hash of the secret. ES can write that annotation to a separate object, but we can also make a small k8s job to patch the deployment when secret changes.

Ben L: quick suggestion — easiest is to add a `dataFrom` sidecar env or add the checksum as `external-secrets.io/refresh-at: <timestamp>` annotation on the secret so we can watch it. But the canonical pattern we use in other services is: in the ExternalSecret controller config, enable `target.metadata.annotations` with `external-secrets.io/last-sync` and then have a deployment `checksum/` annotation generated in our helm chart via the secret's data hash.

Alex K: sounds like we need to update the payments helm chart to compute checksum from the secret and put it on the pod template. can we do that purely in TF/Helm values?

Priya S: helm template can compute values but not the secret contents at render time (since secret comes from ES at runtime). easiest: update ES target to write a `metadata.annotations: { "external-secrets.hash": "$${ES_HASH}" }` — ExternalSecrets supports `target.template` with annotations mapping. then modify deployment to include `checksum/external-secrets: {{ .ObjectMeta.Annotations.external-secrets.hash | default "" }}` — or simpler: have a small post-sync job that runs `kubectl rollout restart`.

Alex K: example patch I tried (works in other clusters):
```yaml
# ExternalSecret target with metadata
spec:
  target:
    name: payments-sa-keys
    template:
      metadata:
        annotations:
          external-secrets.hash: "{{ .Result.Meta.version }}"
```

Tara M: note: that `{{ .Result.Meta.version }}` is controller template interpolation (supported in our controller version?). check controller v0.6+ docs. if not available, we can use `{{ .Checksum }}`.

Sam R: alternative quick fix: run this to force rollout after ES sync (manual):
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/payments -n payments
```
I'll do it now on staging.

devops-bot: Job run: staging-rollout/payments-restart triggered by Sam R — status: started

Ben L: also check RBAC: when TF removed the original secret resource, did we remove any rolebindings that let the deployment's SA read the secret? ES creates the secret in namespace but check `kubectl get secret payments-sa-keys -n payments -o yaml` and confirm `type: Opaque` and `data` present.

Alex K: checked secret exists and has `credentials` key with new value. RBAC looks fine.

Sam R: staging rollout done — pods restarted and new env shows rotated creds. I'd recommend adding a simple `postSync` hook in the ES controller to patch deployment. For production, we should add a Helm value `secretRestartOnChange: true` which will render an `helm.sh/hook` job to do the patch automatically when secret changes.

Priya S: for TF/infra change: update module `k8s/helm-values/payments` -> add value `secret.restartOnChange: true` and a note in the README. also ping @infra-oncall if we change restart behaviour for prod.

Alex K: thanks. I'll: 1) add annotation template to ES to emit a checksum, 2) update helm values to include a checksum annotation reference in `deployment.spec.template.metadata.annotations`, 3) add a short entry in infra README. will open a quick PR for the helm change and link the TF change.

Ben L: SGTM. also add integration test in our k8s smoke suite that rotates the secret and asserts pods pick up new env within 2 minutes.

Alex K: adding that to my TODOs. PRs incoming. thanks all :thumbsup:
